title: Perfect quotient coefficient exchange with augmentation and completion-unit normalization
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal, $A_n=A/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, and $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y)$ a morphism of topoi presented by sites small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Write $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$ for the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $u^*\dashv P=Ru_*$ for the canonical derived adjunction, with counit $\varepsilon$ and ordinary derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Use the completion reflector $C_T$ with unit $\eta_T$ and the full derived-complete subcategory of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]; thus $C_TV=R\lim_n(V\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_T)$ and $u_c^*=C_{\mathcal X}u^*\dashv P$ on complete objects. Put $J=\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and use the small diagram sites of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Their constant ring sheaves are $\Delta\underline A_T$ and their quotient ring sheaves are $B_T=(\underline{A_n}_T)_n$ with the actual quotient transitions. A $B_T$-module system consists of module sheaves $M_n$ over $\underline{A_n}_T$ and $\underline{A_{n+1}}_T$-linear transition maps to $M_n$ by restriction of scalars. Write $U_T$ for restriction to constant-$A$ towers, $S_T=-\otimes^L_{\Delta\underline A_T}B_T$, $\mathcal R_T=S_T\Delta$, and $i_V:\Delta V\to U_T\mathcal R_TV$ for the quotient augmentation. Write $G=u^*$ termwise, $P^J=Ru_*^J$ for derived termwise direct image on constant-$A$ towers, $G_B\dashv P_B$ for the quotient-ring diagram adjunction, and $\mathcal L_T=R\lim$ on constant-$A$ towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. All derived adjunctions are the ones induced from the module adjunctions, not separately chosen hom-set bijections. Assume each $A_n$ is represented over $A$ by a bounded complex of finitely generated projective modules. For every $F\in D_{\mathcal X}$ let$$h_F:\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}(PF)\longrightarrow P_B\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}F$$be the coefficient-exchange mate whose transpose, under $G_B\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}\cong\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}u^*$, is $S_{\mathcal X}\Delta(\varepsilon_F)$. Let $\chi_F:\Delta PF\xrightarrow{\sim}P^J\Delta F$ be the constant-tower comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-tower-pushforward-normalization], and let $h^A_F:U_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}(PF)\to P^JU_{\mathcal X}\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}F$ be the strict-tower projection mate of [lem-weil-pbc-augmented-diagram-projection-mate] for $u$, the object $F$ and the algebra tower $(\underline{A_n}_{\mathcal Y})_n$, with source identified through $\chi_F$. Under the canonical derived-composition comparison $d:U_{\mathcal Y}P_B\cong P^JU_{\mathcal X}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] one has $d\,U_{\mathcal Y}(h_F)=h^A_F$. The quotient-linear evaluation of $h_F$ at $n$ is a map$$h_{F,n}:(PF)\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_{\mathcal Y}\longrightarrow Ru_{*,A_n}(F\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_{\mathcal X})$$whose restriction to $A$ is the $n$-th evaluation of $h^A_F$, the ordinary counit-defined projection for the constant perfect coefficient $\underline{A_n}$. The maps $h_F$ and $h_{F,n}$ are natural isomorphisms. With the direct-image/limit comparison $a$ of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] and the identifications $\mathcal L_TU_T\mathcal R_T=C_T$ of [lem-pur-strict-quotient-diagonal-normalization], define$$\rho_F=a_{U_{\mathcal X}\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}F}^{-1}\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(h^A_F):C_{\mathcal Y}PF\longrightarrow PC_{\mathcal X}F.$$Then $\rho_F\eta_{\mathcal Y,PF}=P(\eta_{\mathcal X,F})$. All transitions in these identities are actual coefficient restrictions. No finite-cardinality assumption on $A_n$, flatness of $A\to A_n$, scheme hypothesis, or completeness of $F$ is imposed.

proof.text: Obtain the normalized quotient-diagram presentation p and common-composite comparison d, with their strict and finite mate identities, from quotientExchangeDiagramNormalization.

The strictExchange component is reductionY.tower.hom, then towerProjection, then towerPush of reductionX.tower.inv. This follows by the adjunction mate counit identity. PerfectStrictReductionProjection makes it an isomorphism. Restriction of exchange followed by d is this component, so conservative derived restriction reflects its invertibility. Quotient evaluation then preserves the resulting natural isomorphism.

Substitute the same strictExchange factorization in completionExchange. Naturality and cancellation of the reductionX tower comparison leave Rlim(towerProjection) followed by directLimitIso inverse. StrictReductionProjectionCompletionUnit proves the claimed completion-unit identity.

lean.statement: theorem perfectQuotientExchangeNormalization [IsNoetherianRing A] (hperfect : PerfectQuotients A I) : ∃ (p : Presentation f A I) (d : p.push.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙ p.atY.restrictionD ≅ p.atX.restrictionD ⋙ f.towerPush A), PresentationNormalized f A I p ∧ d.hom = restrictionMate p ∧ (∀ F : X.derived A, p.atY.restrictionD.map ((exchange p).app F) ≫ d.hom.app (p.atX.reductionD.obj F) = (strictExchange p).app F) ∧ (∀ (F : X.derived A) (n : ℕ), (finiteExchange p n).app F = f.finiteProjection A I n F) ∧ (∀ (F : X.derived A) (n : ℕ), (Y.evaluate A n).map ((strictExchange p).app F) ≫ (Y.evaluate A n).map ((f.towerPush A).map (p.reductionX.tower.hom.app F)) ≫ (f.evaluatePushIso A n).hom.app ((X.reduction A I).obj F) ≫ (f.push A).map ((X.finiteEvaluationIso A I n).hom.app F) ≫ (f.finiteRestrictionPushIso A I n).hom.app ((X.finiteReduction A I n).obj F) = (Y.evaluate A n).map (p.reductionY.tower.hom.app ((f.push A).obj F)) ≫ (Y.finiteEvaluationIso A I n).hom.app ((f.push A).obj F) ≫ (Y.finiteRestriction A I n).map ((finiteExchange p n).app F)) ∧ IsIso (exchange p) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (finiteExchange p n)) ∧ (∀ F : X.derived A, (Y.unit A I).app ((f.push A).obj F) ≫ completionExchange p F = (f.push A).map ((X.unit A I).app F))
